cues: Interference comes from waves from two separate coherent sources.
Diffraction comes from wavelets from different parts of the same wavefront.
Interference fringes are equally wide and equally bright.
In diffraction, the central band is twice as wide as the rest, and the intensity falls off fast.
And the formulas: for interference, a path difference of n lambda gives brightness.
For a single slit, a sine theta equals n lambda gives darkness.
text: Interference comes from waves from two separate coherent sources. Diffraction comes from wavelets from different parts of the same wavefront. Interference fringes are equally wide and equally bright. In diffraction, the central band is twice as wide as the rest, and the intensity falls off fast. And the formulas: for interference, a path difference of n lambda gives brightness. For a single slit, a sine theta equals n lambda gives darkness.
